text:
[Adaptive Hardness Negative Sampling (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709) argues for adjusting negative difficulty during training rather than always selecting the highest-scoring items, mitigating both false-positive and false-negative effects. Its evidence concerns collaborative filtering; transfer to masked BERT4Rec remains an experimental hypothesis. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compares random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling, providing relevant comparison designs rather than evidence that harder negatives universally win.

[Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) identifies a sampled-softmax bias: the positive is included deterministically, whereas negatives are sampled. Its revised correction introduces a model-uncertainty weight and reports improvements over standard logQ correction. This concerns sampling bias, not identification of genuinely disliked items; high model scores alone cannot distinguish informative negatives from unobserved positives.

For this task, a defensible single-model hypothesis is uniform warm-up followed by a mixture of uniform and moderately hard candidates scored by the same BERT4Rec network, excluding known training positives and limiting extreme-negative influence. These are proposed adaptations, not established results for this benchmark. Compare against uniform K=16 and a larger uniform pool to separate candidate-count gains from selection gains; retain masked-target training and appended-mask inference. Missing diagnostic margins do not establish a need for harder negatives. Select using the fixed macro validation HR@10 and training cost, with one checkpoint per category.
